summary: Literal branding takes people as indexed patients or an overt buttocks NP. Preterit Tməġluxli has agent -lux and patient -li; tmiġile has a third-person agent and plural patient marking.

The new figurative subsense is restricted to explicit wordplay: heated seal is rejected, the man's lower seal is requested, nikole names intercourse, and the woman resumes it as stamping. The earlier Imperativ need not already bear that figurative meaning.
The Turkish-derived base supports ordinary Turoyo Infectum, Imperativ and now a source-backed Preterit box. No light verb is involved.
The existing Infectum example matches the PrS 26/21 consent wording despite being cited prs 63/34; numbering must be checked before a citation change.
Is the sexual use at PrS 10/11 conventional beyond this story, or a one-off euphemistic wordplay? The added subsense is explicitly restricted to that context.
